strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this 3.619km layout, with the high-speed corners putting immense stress on the rubber.
The pit window is likely to be between laps 18 and 22, depending on the tire strategy and race pace.
Fuel consumption will be a concern, particularly in the early stages of the race, with drivers needing to manage their fuel load carefully.
An early safety car could throw the strategy books out the window, forcing teams to react quickly and decisively.
The shorter International layout means slightly less fuel consumption compared to the full Grand Prix circuit, allowing for potentially more aggressive strategies.
Undercutting will be a powerful tool, with the relatively short lap time making it easier to gain track position in the pits.
The key will be finding the right balance between pace and tire management, a delicate act that could determine the outcome of the race.
With only 11 turns, the importance of straight-line speed is amplified, making DRS effectiveness crucial for overtaking.
